headline: LPA Development Chance Rises to Medium as Trough Brings Rain to Eastern Visayas, Parts of Mindanao
seoTitle: LPA Development Chance Rises to Medium; Trough Brings Rain | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA says an LPA 1,805 km east of Eastern Visayas now has a medium chance of becoming a tropical depression within 24 hours, while its trough brings rain to parts of Visayas and Mindanao.
deck: The monitored system remains outside PAR, but PAGASA has raised its 24-hour development potential from low to medium and warns its trough can produce moderate to at times heavy rain over Eastern Visayas, Caraga, Bohol and Davao Oriental.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What changed
paragraphs: PAGASA said the low pressure area being monitored east of the Philippines was about 1,805 kilometers east of Eastern Visayas as of 2 a.m. Tuesday, September 22, still outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility.

The agency now assesses the system as having a medium potential to develop into a tropical depression within the next 24 hours. That is a material change from PAGASA's low 24-hour development assessment reported Monday.

sections.heading: Rain is already affecting parts of the country
paragraphs: PAGASA forecasts cloudy skies with scattered rains and thunderstorms over Eastern Visayas, Caraga, Bohol and Davao Oriental because of the LPA's trough. Moderate to at times heavy rain may trigger flash floods or landslides.
Palawan and Occidental and Oriental Mindoro remain affected by the southwest monsoon, while localized thunderstorms may affect the rest of the country.

sections.heading: What is confirmed
paragraphs: The LPA remains outside PAR and is not yet a tropical cyclone. Its increased development potential and the rainfall forecast are confirmed in PAGASA's September 22 early-morning weather bulletin and independently reported by GMA News and the Philippine News Agency.

sections.heading: What remains uncertain
paragraphs: A medium development potential is not a declaration that a tropical depression will form. Entry into PAR, the eventual track, intensity and any later direct impacts remain subject to succeeding PAGASA analyses.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: The system has progressed from a distant monitored LPA with low short-term development potential to one whose trough is already contributing to rain over parts of the Visayas and Mindanao while its near-term development probability has increased.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch PAGASA for whether the LPA enters PAR, whether it develops into a tropical depression, and whether rainfall or tropical-cyclone advisories are escalated.

verificationNotes: PAGASA is the primary authority for the system's status and forecast.
PNA and GMA independently report the 1,805-kilometer position, medium 24-hour development potential and rainfall areas from PAGASA's early-morning bulletin.

This is published as a continuation of FMB News' September 21 LPA report because the short-term development probability increased from low to medium and the trough is now forecast to produce scattered rain in specified areas.
The article does not call the system a tropical cyclone or state that PAR entry has occurred.
The contextual satellite image is reused from the earlier FMB report with the same verified licensing and is explicitly labeled as archival rather than current imagery.
